findings.title: Default value `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition time, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the module is first imported, and that single timestamp becomes the default for all future instances. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` argument will share the same stale timestamp (the time of module import). The fix is to use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` from the `dataclasses` module, which calls the function fresh for each instance. While the `queued` field isn't currently used in comparison logic in this PR, it will produce incorrect data and will silently break any future logic that relies on it.
